title: MCP: edit and delete a document tool (ChangeTool, DeleteTool)
body:
**What's missing:** a document tool can be added over MCP (`add_tool`), but it can't be edited or deleted. The tool editor's commands are `ChangeTool` (replace the definition, so ops on the tool turn stale) and `DeleteTool` (remove it; undo restores its number and body), both in `crates/app/src/commands/tool.rs`. A headless agent that needs a longer stickout, a different flute count or another rpm has to add a second tool under a new name and re-point every op with `set_tool`. A tool added by mistake can only go by `undo`.

**Neighbour that works:** `edit_operation { name, params }` applies a JSON merge patch over an op's fields, refuses an unknown field by name, and runs `EditOperationParams` (`crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs`).

**Done means:**
- `edit_tool { name, definition }` applies a JSON merge patch over the tool's `get_job` definition, refuses an unknown field by name, and runs `ChangeTool` through `env.history`, one undo step. The command's own refusals come back as tool errors: non-finite or non-positive numbers, a retype the tool law refuses for an op using the tool, a body that no longer fits.
- `delete_tool { name }` runs `DeleteTool`, one undo step. The reply names any operations that still use the tool.
- In-process JSON-RPC tests pin both: an edit makes the op stale, undo restores it, and the refusals are named. They also cover what verify and post do once a used tool is gone.

Labels per AGENTS.md for an agent-filed issue: `enhancement`, `P2`, `area:ui`, `source:agent` (this account can't set labels).

title: MCP: state the workpiece material and apply the feeds-and-speeds suggestion (SetWorkMaterial, ApplyCuttingData)
body:
**What's missing:** the Cutting data page's feeds and speeds (M13.2) can't be reached over MCP. The page states the workpiece material (`SetWorkMaterial`, `crates/app/src/commands/cutting_data.rs`), reads the table's suggestion for an operation (`cutting::suggest`), and applies it in one undo step (`ApplyCuttingData`: the op's feed and the tool's rpm). A headless agent has to pick feed and spindle speed by hand through `edit_operation` and `add_tool`'s definition, or post with the catalog defaults, whatever the material is.

**Neighbour that works:** in the GUI, the page shows `cutting::suggest`'s numbers and its Apply button queues `ApplyCuttingData`. That command refuses by name when the op already runs the suggestion, and when the kind has no milling feed.

**Done means:**
- `set_work_material { material }` runs `SetWorkMaterial` through `env.history`. `material` is the project file's word (`aluminium_6061`, `mild_steel`, `stainless_304`, `grey_cast_iron`, `brass`, `plastics_pom`), or `null` to clear it.
- `suggest_cutting_data { operation }` returns the suggestion as data, writing nothing: material, tool material, cutting speed, feed per tooth, thinning factor, rpm, feed, and the machine clamps applied.
- `apply_cutting_data { operation }` runs `ApplyCuttingData`, one undo step, and returns what it applied.
- `get_job` shows the document's work material.
- The commands' refusals come back as tool errors: no material stated, an unknown material word, a kind with no milling feed, an op already on the suggestion.
- In-process JSON-RPC tests pin it.

Labels per AGENTS.md for an agent-filed issue: `enhancement`, `P2`, `area:ui`, `source:agent` (this account can't set labels).

title: MCP: move an operation to another setup, and delete a setup (SetOperationSetup, DeleteSetup)
body:
**What's missing:** the MCP server can add and activate setups (`add_setup`, `activate_setup`), but it can't move an operation into another setup or delete a setup. Both are app commands the GUI uses: `SetOperationSetup` (`crates/app/src/commands/setup.rs`) and `DeleteSetup` (`crates/app/src/commands/setup_delete.rs`). A headless agent that put an op in the wrong setup, or added one setup too many, can only `undo` back to that point and redo the work after it.

**Neighbour that works:** `add_setup` / `activate_setup` (`crates/app/src/mcp/setup_tools.rs`) run `CreateSetup` / `ActivateSetup` through the History.

`DeleteSetup` already refuses a setup that still machines operations, with `'<op>' machines in '<setup>' - move or delete it first`. Over MCP, half of that advice has no tool to follow it.

**Done means:**
- `set_operation_setup { operation, setup }` runs `SetOperationSetup` through `env.history`. `setup` is a declared setup, or null for the implicit first position. The command keeps the stamp, so the op reads `ok` or `stale` by the staleness law.
- `delete_setup { name }` runs `DeleteSetup`. It takes the setup's private furniture with it, and one undo restores them.
- Both return what changed. The commands' refusals come back as tool errors: an unknown op or setup, a move to where the op already is, a setup an op still machines in, and a setup another one is placed relative to.
- In-process JSON-RPC tests pin it: moving an op between two setups, deleting the emptied setup, undo and redo, and the refusals.

Labels per AGENTS.md for an agent-filed issue: `enhancement`, `P2`, `area:ui`, `source:agent` (this account can't set labels).

title: MCP: set and read a tool's controller number (SetToolNumber)
body:
**What's missing:** a tool's controller number (`SetToolNumber`, #221, `crates/app/src/commands/tool_number.rs`) can't be set or read over MCP. That number is the `T..` / `H..` a post writes, and it has to match the machine's tool table. A headless agent's tools always post as their position in the document's tool list. On `main` ed24aead, a job that adds EM-1000-4FL, EM-0600-4FL and DR-0300 posts EM-1000-4FL as `T03` (its place in the sorted list), whatever pocket it sits in on the machine. `get_job`'s tool rows don't show the number either, so the agent can't see what will be posted.

**Neighbour that works:** the GUI's tool editor sets it through `SetToolNumber` (one undo step). Refused by name: an unknown or non-tool name, a number outside 1-99999, a number another tool already has, and a no-op. `tool_numbers::numbers` gives every tool the number it posts as.

**Done means:**
- A `set_tool_number { tool, number }` tool runs `SetToolNumber` through `env.history`. `number` is an integer, or `null` to go back to the list position.
- It returns the tool's own number and the number it posts as.
- `get_job`'s tool rows gain `number` (the tool's own, or null) and `posts_as`.
- The command's refusals come back as tool errors.
- In-process JSON-RPC tests pin it: a renumbered tool posts as that `T` word, undo puts the old number back, and the refusals are named.

Labels per AGENTS.md for an agent-filed issue: `enhancement`, `P2`, `area:ui`, `source:agent` (this account can't set labels).

title: MCP: lay the part on a picked face (AlignPartToSetup::lay_on_plane, #330)
body:
**What's missing:** the Setups page lays the part on a G17/G18/G19 plane by one picked flat face (#330, `AlignPartToSetup::lay_on_plane`, `crates/app/src/commands/setup_align.rs`), but the MCP server has no tool for it. A headless agent can lay a part on three picked points (`lay_part_on_points`, #555) and turn it in the plane (`set_part_axes`, #557). Laying a face down means picking three of its vertices, or computing the quaternion for `set_wcs` by hand.

**Neighbour that works:** `lay_part_on_points` (`crates/app/src/mcp/align_tools.rs`). It runs `AlignPartToSetup::lay_on_points` through the History: one undo step, refusals by name. `lay_on_plane` and `lay_on_points` share one apply path (`pick::lay_datum`); only the datum differs: a face gives its outward normal and centroid, three points their plane.

**Done means:**
- A `lay_part_on_face { face, setup?, plane?, flip?, place? }` tool takes one `list_features` face id, with the same `plane` / `flip` / `place` options as `lay_part_on_points`. It runs `AlignPartToSetup::lay_on_plane` through `env.history`, one undo step.
- It returns the setup, the stored alignment, and its plain description.
- The command's own refusals come back as tool errors, by name: an edge, a vertex, a curved or degenerate face, more than one face, a pick off the part, and a lay the setup already holds.
- In-process JSON-RPC tests pin it: a box laid on a side face changes how the setup holds the part, undo and redo work, and each refusal is named.

Labels per AGENTS.md for an agent-filed issue: `enhancement`, `P2`, `area:ui`, `source:agent` (this account can't set labels).

title: Machines: Sienci AltMill (2×4, 4×4, 4×8) on the SLB-EXT, posting through the grblHAL post
body:
Add machine definitions, and the post they need, for Sienci Labs' AltMill CNC routers, driven by the SLB-EXT controller. **There are three sizes:**

| | AltMill 2×4 | AltMill 4×4 | AltMill 4×8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Work area (X × Y) | ~25 × 49 in | ~49 × 49 in (1265 × 1251 mm) | ~49.8 × 104 in (1265 × 2640 mm) |
| Z travel | ~5.5 in | ~5.5 in (one page: 174 mm) | ~210 mm |
| Max cutting speed | ~590-600 IPM | ~590-600 IPM | ~1,000 IPM Y, ~590 IPM X |
| Spindle | none included: 80 mm mount; optional 2.2 kW ER20 spindle, or the 2.2 kW ATC spindle | as 2×4 | as 2×4 |
| Rotary (optional) | Vortex rotary axis on the SLB-EXT's A output | as 2×4 | as 2×4 |
| Motion | NEMA 23 closed-loop steppers | as 2×4 | as 2×4 |

The figures come from Sienci's product and resources pages, which disagree with each other in places (the 4×4's Z: 5.5 in vs 174 mm; X and Y speeds). Confirm each figure against Sienci's current spec page or manual before committing a `.mch` (see Done means).

**Controller:** the SLB-EXT is a 32-bit board running **grblHAL**, usually driven by Sienci's gSender. That makes this post a grblHAL dialect, built on the grblHAL post in #710 (PR #715) rather than written from scratch.

**No new post file.** The AltMill machine files use `grblhal.cps` from #710, the way all the Tormach mills share `tormach.cps`. A separate `altmill.cps` is added only if something below cannot be a machine-file setting or a grblHAL post option. As of PR #715, the grblHAL post already does what an ATC needs: a plain `T<n> M6` on a line of its own, no G49 (the controller's measured tool length is kept), a `G53 G0 Z` lift when the machine file states `safe_retract` (the AltMill homes), and the first move after a change goes to XY before Z.

**Requirements** (on the machine files, or as small additions to the grblHAL post):
- **Tool change:** the most AltMill-specific part. The post must not depend on the sender: AltMill owners use gSender, and also alternatives such as ncSender. Two modes:
  - *Manual*: the sender intercepts `M6` and runs its own tool-change routine (pause, probe, and so on).
  - *ATC (firmware-handled)*: a `TC.macro` on the SLB-EXT runs `M6 Tn` inside grblHAL, which is transparent to the sender. This covers Sienci's ATC spindle and the **RapidChange ATC** ([rcatc-scripts-grblhal](https://github.com/greilick-industries/rcatc-scripts-grblhal): `TC.macro` runs on every `M6` with a valid tool, settings in `P200.macro`, grblHAL core 20240506 or newer).
  - In both modes the post emits a plain `M6 Tn` on a line of its own, as #710 already plans, with the length offset on the next line. It adds no sender-specific comments or macros, because some gSender versions reportedly rewrite `M6T1` even in passthrough.
  - A post option picks manual or ATC. With ATC, the machine file states the rack's pocket count and which tool numbers it holds, and any other tool is a manual change or a refusal by name. The tool length comes from the ATC's own measurement, so the post does not ask for a manual touch-off after an ATC change.
- **Units:** most AltMill users work in inches. The post honours G20/G21 from the setup and never mixes them.
- **Spindle:** the spindle is bought separately, so the machine file carries a default spindle (the 2.2 kW ER20, 24,000 rpm max, to be checked against Sienci's kit page) that the user can change. `S` words are clamped to the stated range, or refused by name if out of range.
- **Rotary (Vortex):** an A-axis rotary along X on the SLB-EXT's dedicated A output (closed-loop Vortex, gSender's "4th Axis Mode"). The older "Rotary Mode", which drives the rotary through the Y output, is not supported and is refused by name. Indexing and wrapping follow #714 and wait on it.
- **Out of scope:** laser (LaserBeam) and plasma add-ons.

**Done means:**
- `assets/machines/sienci-altmill-2x4.mch`, `sienci-altmill-4x4.mch` and `sienci-altmill-4x8.mch` exist, with travels, axis speeds, the default spindle and the rotary option. Every figure is sourced from Sienci's spec page or manual and cited in the decision file.
- All three are registered in `posting::MACHINES`, with tests in the style of the Tormach machine tests.
- The AltMill machines post through `grblhal.cps`, with goldens under `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/grblhal/` for a small pocket with a tool change on an AltMill machine, in both inch and mm. With an ATC rack stated, a tool outside the rack is handled as above. Any change needed in `grblhal.cps` keeps its existing goldens byte-exact.
- Without #714, any A word is refused by name. Once #714 lands, the Vortex is covered by its indexing goldens.
- The post passes a sender run and a real-machine dry run before it is trusted. I have an AltMill with an SLB-EXT, a RapidChange ATC and ncSender, and can run the goldens on that setup (ATC mode, ncSender).

Depends on: #710 (grblHAL post). Related: #714 (grblHAL 4th axis), #707 (similar machine + post request).

Suggested labels (filed from outside, cannot set them): enhancement, P2, area:post, source:agent.

title: Viewport origin gizmos should name themselves
body:
With several setups on screen, every origin triad looks alike - nothing in the viewport says whose zero is whose. Hover answers "what is this" only one gizmo at a time; the ask is to read it at a glance, and in a screenshot that goes onto a setup sheet.

**Shape wanted:** every origin gizmo labels itself at its origin. Each work-offset triad draws the entity name the Setup pane already uses (`G54` for the first setup, `Setup2/WCS` for the second) just below its projected origin, in a bright label color at the ordinary overlay-label size; the dimmed neutral world axes draw `World` in the same dim gray as their lines. Names ride `gizmos()`: always visible, and an offset hidden by the Models-pane eye - or the world-axes toggle - loses its name with its lines, so no label clutter survives a hidden gizmo. Only the axis-tip `X`/`Y`/`Z` letters keep the big font.

**Considered and dropped:** hover-only labels (not readable at a glance or screenshottable); per-tip offset glyphs (`G54 triad X` - six-plus glyphs per gizmo, clutter that buries the axes); coloring each offset's whole triad by setup (the axes' RGB channels already carry axis meaning).

**Already built:** PR #645 implements exactly this, pinned by `gizmo_tests` (world axes labeled `World`, each triad labeled with its own offset name, name stands at the origin not the tips, hidden offsets drop their names). This issue exists so that PR has the right number to close: the review on #645 caught that it cited #641 - the unrelated lathe grooving bug - by mistake.

title: fixture_library test fails on Windows: Unix-style paths aren't absolute there

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
What happens: the batch tier on main (f42d3788, Windows) is red on one test. It is `crates/app/tests/fixture_library.rs`, `the_library_folder_is_the_override_else_a_sibling_of_machines` (1635 passed, 1 failed). Every other lane is green, clippy included.

```
panicked at crates\app\tests\fixture_library.rs:117:5:
  left: None
 right: Some("/shop/fixtures")
```

Cause: the test feeds Unix paths (`/shop/fixtures`, `/Users/me`) to `fixture_library::user_dir_for("macos", …)`. `crates/app/src/fixture_library/store.rs:32` keeps an override only if `PathBuf::is_absolute()`, and that test runs on the host OS. On Windows `/shop/fixtures` has no drive letter, so it isn't absolute and is dropped. The test likely passes on Linux and macOS.

Came from: a3c859bd (fixture library, #339), merged via d0f0a80b. Nothing has touched the file since.

Fix options: make the test's paths host-absolute (built from `std::env::temp_dir()` or `cfg!(windows)` pairs), or have `user_dir_for` judge absoluteness by the target OS string it is given, not by the host. Check how the machine-library sibling (`user_dir_for` there, if any) handles it and match it.

Done means: `fixture_library` passes on Windows and the batch tier is green on main.

title: main does not build lathe_thread_travel: OpParams::Threading literal is missing the new hand field
body:
`cargo test -p camcraft-app` does not build on `main` b57f8d52: one test binary fails to compile.

```
error[E0063]: missing field `hand` in initializer of `OpParams`
  --> crates\app\tests\lathe_thread_travel.rs:83:18
error: could not compile `camcraft-app` (test "lathe_thread_travel") due to 1 previous error
```

**Reproduction** (Windows, stable toolchain, main b57f8d52):

```
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test lathe_thread_travel --no-run
```

Every other `camcraft-app` test binary and `camcraft-cli` build. A plain `cargo test -p camcraft-app` stops at this error, so it runs nothing.

**Root cause (confirmed):** two PRs merged cleanly in text but not in meaning.
- #643 (merge 855a91f9) added `crates/app/tests/lathe_thread_travel.rs`, which builds an `OpParams::Threading { .. }` literal.
- #639 (merge feee7e59, later) added the `hand` field to `OpParams::Threading` and updated the existing literals (`inverted_post.rs`, `lathe_field_tools.rs`, ...), but not the one in the new file.

**Fix:** add `hand: camcraft_app::cl::ThreadHand::Right` to that literal (a right-hand thread, which is what the test's bar and insert describe). No product code changes.

Done means: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test lathe_thread_travel` builds and its tests pass on main.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.

title: Model page: a part turn or move runs no stock/part-vs-fixture interpenetration check

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found in the review of PR #576 (#571).

**Today:** locate (#561, PR #566) warns by name when the part or its stock would sink into a fixture. A plain Model-page `MoveModel` (move or turn) runs no such check. Since #571 (PR #576) a turned part's square stock is refitted around it, so the regrown block could enter a vise jaw or floor with no warning. The old rigid tilt had the same gap, so this is not a regression.

**Expected:** `MoveModel` runs the same sampled part-and-stock-versus-fixture check as locate and warns by name: the moved body, the fixture and a point. A warning, not a refusal, as with locate.

**Done means:** a test moves or turns a part so its stock enters a fixture and gets the by-name warning; a clear move gets none.

title: Model page: turning a part with a square stock tilts the stock (MoveModel rotates the stock rigidly)

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found while fixing #561 (PR #566).

**Today:** turning a part on the Model page by an angle that isn't a quarter turn rotates its box or cylinder stock rigidly with it (`crates/app/src/commands/move_model.rs:105-108`). A stock square to the machine ends up tilted, and ops then cut a tilted blank's top. #566 fixed this for locate only (`stock_follow.rs`: a stock square to the setup keeps its orientation and is refitted with each side's allowance). Plain `MoveModel` keeps the rigid follow, and `commands_undo::moving_one_part_carries_existing_stock_and_undo_restores_both` pins it.

**Expected:** decide whether a Model-page turn should use the same square-stock rule. Likely yes: a vise clamps the blank square. If it changes, the existing pin is updated with the decision recorded.

**Done means:** a test turns a part with a square stock by 30° on the Model page and checks the stock stays square, or the rigid behaviour is kept and documented with a by-name note to the user.
